subject: Post-call: Procurement readiness & pricing path (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
messages:
--- Message 1: Marissa Cole to Aurora Pay (post-call recap) ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@aurorapay.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@aurorapay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Procurement readiness & pricing path (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Hi Jared / Samira —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum for your Q2 pilot procurement: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: payment reconciliation and fraud signal enrichment (latency SLO ~200ms p95)
- Data requirements: PII redaction in-flight, audit logs for 12 months
- Purchasing rules: prefer PO for anything > $50k; procurement team will route to finance for net-45; Marketplace listing is desirable for faster procurement but not required

Commercial paths we discussed (please confirm preference)
1) Hosted (Redwood API) — on-demand or committed monthly usage; fastest onboarding; good for initial pilot
2) Dedicated — reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput; recommended if you need sustained concurrency and tight latency SLOs
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — for longer-term regulated workloads; involves legal/infra coordination and longer lead time

Open questions / asks for procurement readiness
- Will Aurora go PO or card for the pilot? (you mentioned PO > $50k; want to confirm the approval cadence)
- Any required vendor paperwork (W-9, SOC2 attestation, custom security questionnaire)?
- Marketplace interest: if procurement prefers marketplace, we can prioritize a listing and provide the marketplace SOW template

Attached: Aurora_Redwood_Pricing_Options_v2.pdf (pricing bands for on-demand vs committed, hosted/dedicated/private notes) and Redwood_Terms_Summary_Mar2026.pdf (summary of standard terms)

Proposed next steps
- You: confirm PO vs card and list of procurement contacts (cc procurement@aurorapay.com if handy) — target by 2026-03-10
- Me: update the pricing ask sheet and push a HubSpot deal note with the marketplace path and estimated timeline — I’ll send a short decision matrix by EOD tomorrow
- Internal: loop legal if Aurora requests custom terms beyond our standard SOW

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: Aurora_Redwood_Pricing_Options_v2.pdf (pdf, 1.1MB)]

--- Message 2: Jared Cole (Aurora Pay) reply ---
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@aurorapay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@aurorapay.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorapay.com
Date: 2026-03-08T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Procurement readiness & pricing path (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick points from procurement/finance perspective: 
- Pilot budget will likely be under $50k which we can charge on card; if the pilot expands past that threshold we will need a PO and lead time for approvals (2–3 weeks).
- Marketplace listing would speed our internal approvals (procurement likes vendor marketplaces), so please share any marketplace intake form or SOW template.
- Security: we will need current SOC2 Type II and a standard security questionnaire (I’ll attach the buyer Q by EOD).

Preferred path for pilot: Hosted (on-demand) to reduce procurement friction. If we see latency issues in the pilot we’ll discuss moving to Dedicated.

Can you send a one-page pricing comparison (hosted on-demand vs 6mo commit vs dedicated baseline) and a simple scorecard we can share with finance? Also include payment terms for PO vs card (net-45 / immediate card charge).

-Jared
Head of Platform Partnerships | Aurora Pay
jared.cole@aurorapay.com
[Procurement gave me the buyer checklist — attaching shortly]

--- Message 3: Marissa internal to Rishi & Aditya (FYI + ask) ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Procurement readiness & pricing path — Aurora Pay (pilot preference: hosted on-demand)

Rishi / Aditya —

Aurora prefers hosted on-demand for the pilot (likely < $50k). Procurement would like marketplace if possible. They requested: SOC2, security questionnaire, and a 1-page comparison + scorecard.

Can we do the following?
- Rishi: draft a 1-page pricing comparison (hosted on-demand vs 6mo commit vs dedicated baseline) + a one-slide scorecard (cost / latency / setup time / procurement friction). Aim for a draft in 24 hours.
- Aditya: can you confirm whether we can expedite marketplace intake? If yes, what lead time do we tell them (estimate in business days)?
- Stephanie: heads-up on likely SOC2 and potential redline items (Aurora mentioned longer retention for audit logs) — can you review the terms summary attached?

I’ll hold off sending the external one-pager until we align internally.

Best,
Marissa

--- Message 4: Rishi Malhotra internal reply ---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Procurement readiness & pricing path — Aurora Pay (pilot preference: hosted on-demand)

Thanks Marissa — I’ll take the one-pager and scorecard. Plan:
- Deliver a concise 1-page comparison that shows list price (on-demand), 6-month committed discount tier (10–15% depending on min commit), and a Dedicated baseline rate with required commit sizing.
- Scorecard will be a 1-slide matrix: cost estimate (30d pilot), expected p95 latency range, onboarding time (days), procurement friction (low/med/high).

Marketplace: I spoke with Marketplace ops — we can do a minimal listing in ~10 business days if we provide the intake form + SOW template. If they want a fully certified marketplace vendor (security attestation + integration) that’s closer to 6–8 weeks.

I’ll send drafts to Marissa for customer-facing review by 2026-03-09T09:00:00-07:00.

-Rishi
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[rishi.malhotra@redwood.com]

--- Message 5: Stephanie Nguyen (Legal) reply (contract redlines note) ---
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Procurement readiness & pricing path — Aurora Pay (pilot preference: hosted on-demand)

Quick legal note —
- SOC2 Type II: we can provide our latest report and a summary of controls. If Aurora requests evidence beyond the SOC2 report (e.g., syslogs), we’ll need to clarify the specific data access request and ensure we have an approved DPA amendment.
- Data retention: standard is 90 days for request-level logs, 12 months for aggregated audit logs. If Aurora needs longer retention for audit, we can discuss a limited-term amendment and associated cost.
- PO vs card: commercial terms are standard; if they sign PO with net-45 we need 2 approvals when > $50k. For pilot under $50k, card is fastest.

I’ll review any redlines they send and propose a redline matrix. For now, go ahead and send the one-pager and scorecard to procurement with the marketplace intake option flagged as "expedite available (10bd)".

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: Redwood_Terms_Summary_Mar2026.pdf]
